## Structure and components

- [statement] Atlas Infinite preview includes 24 hours of continuous backup without an additional backup charge; longer retained history is billed hourly as backup storage. Internal storage-layer replication is excluded from transfer billing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers
- [statement] Atlas Infinite documentation includes a 24-hour continuous-backup window without additional backup cost; longer retention is billed. Storage-layer replication, backup, and recovery traffic does not count toward transfer charges. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Enabling continuous backup changes the billing schedule for combined snapshot and oplog storage. The cost difference from ordinary snapshot pricing depends on storage volume, provider and region: the free first 5 GB can make continuous backup cheaper for small backup sets, while the documented AWS us-east-1 example with 115 GB costs $106.25 per month rather than $16.10 at the flat snapshot rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/continuous-backup-billing-calculation/272197, https://www.ohchimp.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-continuous-backup-costs
- [statement] MongoDB recommends co-locating applications with the cluster's provider and region, projecting only needed fields, and enabling driver network compression to reduce transfer costs. This targets returned bytes and network paths rather than proving savings from any particular query plan. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers
- [statement] Backup invoices use GB-days rather than just GB; daily storage quantities must be interpreted with the applicable backup schedule and tier rates. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/continuous-backup-billing-calculation/272197

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas pricing has distinct cluster, backup, and data-transfer cost categories. Estimating cost solely from instance size omits backup and transfer usage. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-mongodb-atlas/costs-licenses.html, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-pricing-explained-what-youre-really-paying-for/, https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/manish-negandhi/2026/04/14/optimizing-mongodb-atlas-cost
- [statement] Dedicated-cluster PITR storage includes snapshots plus an internal oplog. Longer restore windows retain more oplog history and raise backup costs; rate schedules depend on provider, region, and usage tier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/backups.md
- [statement] Snapshots are generally incremental. Deleting one snapshot does not release blocks still referenced by retained snapshots. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.ohchimp.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-continuous-backup-costs
- [statement] Node changes, failover, configuration changes, and cloud-provider maintenance can require additional full snapshots. Atlas-performed maintenance, including version updates, does not itself require a full snapshot. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.ohchimp.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-continuous-backup-costs
- [statement] Additional regional backup copies incur storage and cross-region transfer charges. Copying every backup to one extra region approximately doubles storage volume; regional rates can differ. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/backups.md
- [statement] Data-transfer cost depends on volume, cloud provider, region, and network path; cross-region replicas add transfer charges. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/manish-negandhi/2026/04/14/optimizing-mongodb-atlas-cost
- [statement] AWS and Google Cloud transfer rules exempt incoming transfers to Atlas and outgoing transfers from Free/Flex clusters. Azure virtual-network peering can charge ingress and egress; free ingress is not a universal rule for every network path. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers
- [statement] In beSharp’s January 2026 Atlas case study, routing a private-subnet application through public endpoints added NAT gateway costs; VPC peering avoided NAT processing while cross-AZ traffic remained chargeable. This conclusion depends on that network topology. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-14) — https://blog.besharp.it/aws-data-transfer-costs-from-a-nutshell-to-the-calculator-through-3-real-world-scenarios/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers
- [statement] Backup frequency and retention should follow recovery objectives: fewer snapshots can reduce storage cost, but PIT restores may need to replay more oplog operations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/backups.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/manish-negandhi/2026/04/14/optimizing-mongodb-atlas-cost
- [statement] Manual HTTPS backup downloads can incur download-VM runtime, restore-volume storage, and transfer charges. Snapshot exports also carry an Atlas per-GB export charge in addition to cloud-provider transfer costs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers
- [statement] Cloud snapshots are usually incremental. Retention and changed data determine stored bytes, so database size multiplied by snapshot count is an unreliable estimate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/backups.md
- [statement] Transfer costs depend on bytes and network placement. Cross-region and Internet-bound egress can add costs beyond cluster compute; the amount depends on cloud provider and source/destination region. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-pricing-explained-what-youre-really-paying-for/
- [statement] Reducing snapshot frequency, retention, restore windows, or regional copies can reduce costs, but the policy must still meet recovery and disaster-resilience requirements. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas backup/PITR and data transfer cost drivers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/backups.md
